title: Object transfer device and corresponding gripper

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.quote: Object transfer device comprising a frame ( 3,20,63,58 ), at least one gripper ( 6,22,22 a, 62,57 a, 57 b ) having a gripper body ( 7,25,45 ) and means of guiding the gripper body with respect to the frame;
features.note: The reference discloses a frame (housing) and a gripper body (containing magnetic elements and jaws) which implies a displaceable magnetic element and pole shoes (jaws) for workpiece contact.
features.refuted: The quote describes a gripper with a frame and gripper body, but does not mention a housing containing a displaceable magnet or pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.quote: The gripper comprises a magnetic element ( 12,32,44,52,56 ) capable, when it is subjected to a magnetic field greater than an efficiency threshold, of exerting a force on at least one mobile jaw.
features.note: The magnetic element is described as being driven along a movement path, implying displacement, and its activation by a magnetic field suggests it moves between gripping and release positions.
features.refuted: The quote describes a magnetic element that exerts force on a mobile jaw when subjected to a magnetic field, not a magnet that is displaceable between gripping and release positions.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: the gripper being equipped with one or more jaws ( 8,28 a, 28 b, 46 ) mobile with respect to the gripper body ( 7,25,45 ).
features.note: The reference discloses jaws that contact the workpiece, which can function as pole shoes, but it does not explicitly state they are 'attached to the housing' or that each jaw has a 'workpiece contact surface' in the sense of a distinct pole shoe.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: The gripper comprises a magnetic element ( 12,32,44,52,56 ) capable, when it is subjected to a magnetic field greater than an efficiency threshold, of exerting a force on at least one mobile jaw.
features.note: The jaws are acted upon by a magnetic field, implying they are part of the magnetic circuit, but the reference does not explicitly describe them as 'designed to guide a magnetic field portion' to a specific contact surface.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not provide any information about the angle of the workpiece contact surface relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.quote: Object transfer device comprising a frame ( 3,20,63,58 ), at least one gripper ( 6,22,22 a, 62,57 a, 57 b ) having a gripper body ( 7,25,45 ) and means of guiding the gripper body with respect to the frame;
features.note: The reference discloses a magnetic gripper with a housing, displaceable magnetic element, and jaws (acting as pole shoes), but it does not specify the contact surface angle relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.

features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or angles on the workpiece contact surface.

features.note: The reference does not describe multiple projections on the jaws or pole shoes.

features.note: The reference does not describe projections or recesses on the pole shoes.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any specific positioning device for the workpiece.

claims.note: The abstract and claim 1 describe an 'Object transfer device' which is a magnetic gripper system.
claims.refuted: The quote describes an object transfer device with a frame and mechanical gripper, not a magnetic gripper system.

claims.quote: Object transfer device comprising: a frame, a gripper including a gripper body, a guiding member adapted to guide the gripper body with respect to the frame;
claims.note: The reference discloses a magnetic gripper (referred to as 'gripper' with a 'magnetic element'), but it does not explicitly mention a 'ferromagnetic workpiece' as part of the system, although it implies handling objects.

This reference describes a gripper that uses a magnetic field to operate jaws for clamping an object, but it does not describe a specific gripping state where a magnet is in a gripping position and a ferromagnetic workpiece is pressed against contact surfaces by magnetic force.

This reference describes a gripper that uses a magnetic field to operate jaws for clamping an object, but it does not describe a specific release state where a magnet is in a release position and a ferromagnetic workpiece is not pressed against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
This reference does not describe projections or their length in relation to the thickness of a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference does not describe a receptacle in the form of a groove.

overall.why: This reference is strongly relevant as it discloses a magnetic object transfer device with a gripper, displaceable magnetic elements, and jaws for clamping, which aligns with many core aspects of the subject invention, particularly in its claims.
